clue.text: Mischievous couple of fellows? One's caught …

parts.note: a man or fellow is a MALE, the first of the pair
F is the abbreviation for fellow, the second of the pair
the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Two men are up to no good, and one of them gets nabbed, the story to be continued.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next one in the surface story only; each clue still has its own answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Malefic is a literary word for causing harm or evil, close to mischievous in its stronger sense.

clue.text: Nearly fall over before beginning to light joint

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards in this down clue
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone nearly trips before lighting up a spliff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' cuts AUTUMN to AUTUM, and 'over' turns that into MUTUA.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutual and joint both describe something shared by two or more parties.

clue.text: "People person" making home for outcasts

indicators.note: making home for means the words house the answer, which sits inside them

explanation.surface: A sociable person sets up a refuge for those shunned by society.
explanation.definitionFit: Lepers were historically shunned and isolated, so the word means social outcasts generally.

clue.text: Prearrange fire on road, slippery

indicators.note: slippery suggests sliding about, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A blaze on an icy road was set up in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: To foreordain is to determine or arrange something beforehand, especially by fate.

clue.text: See 21
… in the act and one fellow's locked up …

indicators.note: something locked up is held inside, so the second piece goes within the first

parts.note: taken as written
a stag is a male, as in a stag party for the men only

explanation.surface: The story continues: a man is caught red-handed and thrown in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Performers who are on stage are in the middle of their act.

clue.text: See 21
Perish from condition — it is the skin going red, black etc, so I've heard

annotationWithheld.why: Perish from condition — it is the skin going red, black etc, so I've heard (4): 'red, black etc' defines SEAS and DISEASE less DIE gives it, but no parse accounts for 'it is the skin going' and 'so I've heard' without a word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Perish from condition — it is the skin going red, black etc, so I've heard

clue.text: Eg 24 19 9 12 25 5 down? The Bill on the way to London

parts.note: a bill is an account, abbreviated a/c
over can mean on top of, as in a cloth over or on a table
going to London is going up in British usage

explanation.surface: A police drama follows the officers on the road to the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references read CONS PIRACY TOPER VERT THE COURSE OF JUSTICE, a conspiracy to pervert the course of justice. The Bill was a British TV police drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Conspiring to pervert justice is the classic example of a concealment or whitewash.

clue.text: They may look like the real thing, not northern; or Esther Rantzen's misplaced

definitions.text: They may look like the real thing

indicators.note: misplaced means the letters are put in the wrong places, a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the letters of this word are taken away from the pool

explanation.surface: Fakes pass for genuine, says the TV presenter, though not in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' signals taking NORTHERN's letters away from OR plus ESTHER RANTZEN'S; 'misplaced' rearranges what is left. Esther Rantzen is a British TV presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz goods are imitations or substitutes standing in for the genuine article.

clue.text: … he's on alcohol and on cannabis, spinning

indicators.note: spinning turns the joined pieces round so they are read backwards

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: The miscreant is both drunk and stoned, his head spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: A toper is a habitual drinker, someone always on the bottle.

clue.text: One usual suspect, judge admitted, is not suspicious

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the single letter goes inside the rearranged letters
suspect read as an adjective means doubtful or unreliable, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: At an identity parade one of the usual suspects, a judge among them, shows no sign of distrust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges ONE USUAL, and 'admitted' puts J inside those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Unjealous means free of jealousy, so not suspicious of a rival; the definition reads as 'is not suspicious' to fit the clue's grammar.

clue.text: She's serving up roast and she is criminal!

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A waitress dishes up a roast, but the cooking is a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges ROAST plus SHE IS. 'serving up' is cryptic: a flight attendant serves food while up in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight attendant waits on passengers aloft, so she serves while up in the sky.

clue.text: Not the colour of 10 eyes it's necessary to cover the …

definitions.text: Not the colour of 10 eyes it's

indicators.note: necessary to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Eyes that are not jealous are not green, so they needn't be covered up.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is UNJEALOUS: jealousy is the green-eyed monster, so unjealous eyes are not green.
explanation.definitionFit: Vert is the heraldic name for green, the colour linked with jealousy.

clue.text: Underwear masking characters in theft, we more generally believe

indicators.note: masking means covering, so the underwear goes around the characters of the next word

parts.note: pants are underwear
a heist is a robbery or theft

explanation.surface: A thief hides loot in his underpants and claims a broader faith.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: theists believe in a god, and pantheists hold a wider belief that god is in everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantheists identify God with the whole universe, a more all-embracing belief than ordinary theism.

clue.text: … plea expressing doubts 5 down that underlie act's rewriting

indicators.note: rewriting means the letters of the words before it are written out again in a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A legal plea questioning fairness rests on a rewritten statute.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 down supplies OF JUSTICE (the end of the linked answer at 21). 'rewriting' rearranges UNDERLIE plus ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots law a declinature is a plea declining a judge's jurisdiction, doubting whether a fair trial can be had.

clue.text: Very Big Apple written up in parish priest's objects of admiration

indicators.note: in places the reversed pieces inside the priest's word

parts.note: a curé is a French parish priest

indicators.note: written up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
the Big Apple is New York, NY

explanation.surface: A priest writes up New York in glowing terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' turns SONY into YNOS, which 'in' places inside CURES.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynosure is a centre of attention or admiration, originally the Pole Star.

clue.text: More than one knife victim's ultimate pain at set-up?

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so the last letter is taken

parts.note: an ache is a pain

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom

explanation.surface: A stabbing victim suffers from a pain caused by a frame-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SET into TES. The hyphenated 'set-up' in the surface is a frame-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Machetes are large broad-bladed knives, so the plural means more than one.

clue.text: Disproportionate moralism: one's fitted up in perjury, beginning and end of it

indicators.note: in places the fitter inside the outer letters
the beginning and end of it means the first and last letters of the word before

parts.note: a rigger is one who fits up rigging or scaffolding

explanation.surface: A preachy type is framed for lying under oath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fitted up' looks like being framed for a crime, but here it is what a rigger does.
explanation.definitionFit: Priggery is the self-righteous behaviour of a prig, excessive moral fussiness.

clue.text: Bringing to 4 rough gem in notorious cases

indicators.note: cases means encloses, so the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: arrant means notorious or out-and-out, as in an arrant knave

indicators.note: rough means unpolished or crude, so the letters are knocked into a new shape

explanation.surface: An uncut jewel turns up in a famous trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 is COURT (part of the linked answer at 21). 'rough' rearranges GEM IN to IGNME, which 'cases' puts inside ARRANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Arraignment is calling an accused person before a court to answer a charge.

clue.text: I take in fast crime on 21 6?

indicators.note: in places the first two pieces inside the word for fast

parts.note: pacy means fast
taken as written
R stands for recipe, Latin for take

explanation.surface: Someone takes in a quick crime on the high seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 6 is HIGH SEAS. R is from recipe, the Latin for 'take' on prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: Piracy is robbery committed at sea, the classic crime on the high seas.

clue.text: Treacherous professor quickly set out the expected scenario

indicators.note: set out means arranged afresh, so the letters are laid out in a new order

parts.note: prof is a quick, shortened form of professor

explanation.surface: A traitorous academic hastily outlines what is likely to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something par for the course is just what one would expect, from golf's standard score.

clue.text: Eminent firm's four characters, time inside, deserved diamonds, they rule

parts.note: eminent means high, as in high office
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: inside puts the single letter within the rearranged letters
characters says the letters of the word are used in a different order

parts.note: just means deserved, as in just deserts
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A distinguished company of four people, after a spell inside, earned their diamonds and now rule the roost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' rearranges FOUR to UROF and 'inside' puts T within it, giving URTOF after CO.
explanation.definitionFit: The High Court of Justice in England gives rulings, so its judges are those who rule.

clue.text: Eg Peter's opening from the back: nothing inside — that smells bad!

indicators.note: inside puts the zero within the example safe

parts.note: peter is criminal slang for a safe, so an example of one is a safe
O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: from the back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal opening into a mine

explanation.surface: A safecracker opens a strongbox from behind, finds it empty, and is disgusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the back' turns ADIT into TIDA. Peter is old underworld slang for a safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Asafoetida is a pungent resin used in Indian cooking and notorious for its foul smell.

clue.text: Paid the bail for a sound woman

indicators.note: sound means as spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: to pay bail for someone is to free them, so freed a

explanation.surface: Someone bailed out a woman of sound character.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Freda is a female first name, so any woman so called fits the bare word in the clue.

clue.text: Reasons for their being behind bars?

definitions.text: Reasons for their being behind bars?

parts.words: Reasons for their being behind bars?
parts.note: reads like reasons for imprisonment; really the arguments against a case and also the convicts held in jail

explanation.definitionFit: Cons are arguments against, and also slang for convicts serving time in prison.

clue.text: See 20
Stick used to support a body of officers

definitions.meaning: a stick or rod carried as a support
the officers of an army unit taken together

explanation.definitionFit: Staff means both a walking stick and the group of officers assisting a commander.

clue.text: Check for bleeding pen letters to old Athenian

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
psi is a Greek letter, so psis are letters an ancient Greek would know

explanation.surface: Someone writes letters to an ancient Greek with a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Stypsis is the action of a styptic, stopping bleeding by contracting tissue.

clue.text: In the constitution of copper, perhaps, he determines when to show hesitation

definitions.text: In the constitution of copper, perhaps, he determines

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
to say can mean to show or indicate, as a clock says the time
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A man decides when to pause in making a point about a policeman's build.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constitution' means makeup: an assayer tests what a metal such as copper is made of; 'copper' looks like a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: An assayer analyses metals and ores to find their composition and purity.
